title: No Need to Change Models for 4.2x Faster Token Output: Tencent Hunyuan Open-Sources Draft Model DFly2 to Specifically Accelerate Hy4 flash

content_html:
Large models speak slowly, mostly because they get stuck in the token-by-token generation stage; Tencent Hunyuan's solution is to leave the model untouched and attach an "accelerator" beside it. On November 26, Hunyuan open-sourced a new-generation draft model, DFly2—it does not replace Hy4 flash, but works like an add-on component. While keeping weights and outputs unchanged, it multiplies token generation speed, with up to a 4.2× speedup on individual benchmarks.

Specifically Targets Sparse Attention Models

DFly2 is designed specifically for DSA-style sparse attention large models and long contexts, and is open-sourced alongside the Hy4 flash weights and complete training code. Its scorecard is impressive: on 19 public benchmark sets, DFly2's acceptance length and speedup ratio are overall better than those of DFlash and DSpark, with even more obvious advantages on long texts and Agentic tasks. Its average speedup ratios are about 12% and 30% higher, respectively, and on Agentic and real-world tasks its acceptance length is also 10.4% ahead.

Extreme "Piggybacking" on the Target Model's Existing Resources

The core design of DFly2 is to reuse the target model to the fullest extent: each draft layer directly shares the KV cache of the corresponding sparse attention layer (KV Share) and up to 2,048 positions selected by the indexer (Index Share). This brings three benefits: each draft token attends to at most about 2K keys, so attention complexity is independent of context length and overhead is fixed; no separate KV cache needs to be maintained, resulting in zero extra VRAM overhead; and it does not participate in prefill, making it friendly to PD separation, with only one last-layer hidden state additionally passed from P to D. The weights and code are now available on GitHub and HuggingFace.
